title: pave-init run state (run-state.json)
description: Single shape authority for a pave-init run's persisted state, realizing the state contract in references/pave-init.pave.yaml. State points; artifacts prove: fields hold positions, statuses, counters, and artifact paths - never artifact content. Per-entry free-text fields declare maxLength caps (references/pave-spec.md section 8.1); an entry that needs more cites an artifact path instead. `notes` is this file's single deliberately unconstrained escape hatch, counted against a whole-file warn threshold of 131072 bytes - scripts/validate_run_state.py warns past it and names the compaction action, never refusing the write. $defs.frontier and $defs.fragment are the shape authorities for the Stage 3 planning files (planning/frontier.yaml and planner draft fragments); scripts/validate_run_state.py --frontier checks instances of them plus the hand rules a shape schema cannot express (see references/planning-layout.md).

fitness_override.description: Free-form record of a not_fit override: original verdict, missing characteristics, user rationale, accepted risks. Intentionally loose.

artifact.description: Path of the persisted exploration/<lens>.md report.

frontier_entries.description: Path of planning/frontier.yaml, which is the authority for entries and their lifecycle; null before Stage 3. Its shape authority is $defs.frontier in this schema; check it with scripts/validate_run_state.py --frontier.

build_units.description: Unit list or a pointer to the section of skill-package-plan.md that enumerates them.

validation_results.description: Path of reviews/validation.md; null before Stage 6.

forward_test_result.description: Path of reviews/forward-test.md; null before the forward test.

note.description: One-line context. Longer content lives in an artifact cited under evidence, never here.

notes.description: Free-form prose home for anything the fields above do not carry. This file's single deliberately unconstrained escape hatch (references/pave-spec.md section 8.1), counted against the whole-file warn threshold declared above.

frontier.title: planning/frontier.yaml
frontier.description: The Stage 3 planning queue. The lead is the only writer. Per-entry free-text fields declare maxLength caps; the frontier-level `notes` is this file's single unconstrained escape hatch, counted against the same 131072-byte whole-file warn threshold as run-state.json. A shape schema cannot express the write-ownership and lifecycle rules; those live in references/planning-layout.md and the hand rules of validate_run_state.py --frontier.

entries.description: One entry per frontier node, keyed by node id.

conflicts.description: The run's conflict register. Conflict ids are lead-assigned here and nowhere else; a planner fragment that mints one is a validator error.

notes.description: Free-form prose home: run lessons, assembly items, scratch notes. This file's single deliberately unconstrained escape hatch, counted against the whole-file warn threshold.

status.description: pending -> pending_dispatched (planner sent) -> planned (draft on disk) -> reviewed (reviewer PASS); stale when a resynchronization touches an interface the entry depends on.

contract.description: Frozen contract reference: a lead-authored contract file for the root, else <parent-draft-path>#<node-id>.

draft.description: Workspace-relative draft path, minted by the lead at dispatch. One path per dispatch, never reused; a redispatch mints a new path. Required from pending_dispatched onward (validator hand rule).

prediction.description: The framing planner's sizing prediction with its one-line rationale; the node's own dispatch confirms or overturns it.

dependencies.description: Sibling entry keys whose frozen interfaces this node consumes. A resynchronization that changes an interface marks every reviewed dependent stale (orchestration/explore-and-plan.md section 4.4).

notes.description: Entry prose: dispatch notes, review summaries, retractions. Capped per entry; content that needs more lives in an artifact cited by path. The frontier-level notes field is the file's one unconstrained escape hatch, not this.

id.description: Lead-assigned, unique across the run. Planners report conflicts without ids; the lead registers and numbers them here.

raised_by.description: Frontier entry key that reported it.

fragment.title: planner draft fragment (*.draft.pave.yaml for a dispatched boundary)
fragment.description: A node planner's draft for one dispatched node: authored child node bodies plus planning marks. The dispatched node's own five-part contract is frozen in the parent draft; the fragment references it via extensions.x_planning and never carries slots for it - a fragment that re-authors its dispatched node under nodes is a validator error. The root skeleton draft is a full profile, not a fragment; validate_pave.py owns it.

name.description: The dispatched node's id. Must not reappear as a key under nodes (validator hand rule).

nodes.description: Authored child node bodies only. Node shape is references/pave.schema.json's authority, not this schema's.

x_planning.description: Planning marks: dispatched_node, frozen_contract_reference (path + node), elaboration verdicts and predictions, evidence questions, interface findings. Intentionally loose - except that no mapping under it may carry an 'id' key in the lead-owned conflict namespace (c<N>): those ids are lead-assigned in frontier.yaml's conflict register; node-local labels (n1, e1, ...) are fine (validator hand rule).
